title: Buy One Get One
description:
The convenience store you go to every night.

Today again — one triangle kimbap, and a card held out at the register. Then she speaks.

"That one's close to expiry, so it's buy one get one. Grab another."

The woman behind the counter. Not a stranger — you'd seen her before. But you'd never heard anything like that.

How long has it been since anyone in Seoul showed you this kind of kindness?
For a moment, the narrow little store felt a different temperature.

choices.text: Say thank you — and ask her name  (connection starting / courage·slight distance)
choices.result_text:
"...Thank you. I'm in here all the time and you always look out for me."
She smiled for the first time. "Kim Daeun. I see you a lot."

A small name, exchanged between two people.
The Seoul night felt, just a little, less cold.

choices.text: Just nod thanks and leave  (focus maintained / warmth missed)
choices.result_text:
{name} gave a small bow and stepped out.
Right now, the only thing in view is ₩3 billion.

Still — the bag with two triangle kimbap in it sat strangely heavy in the hand.

title: Regular
description:
She has {name}'s order memorized now. Triangle kimbap, sometimes cup ramyeon.
The late-night convenience store has become a small world just for the two of them.
Tonight, out of nowhere, she says something.
"I'm saving up to bring my mom here. She's alone back in the countryside.
I knew Seoul was expensive, but... not like this."

A life carrying the same weight as {name}'s — and it had been right there behind the counter all along.

choices.text: Genuinely cheer her on — and pitch in when you can  (connection / money·time)
choices.result_text:
{name} helped carry her bags sometimes, and left a warm drink now and then.
Nothing big — but they'd become people who understood each other's exhaustion.
Deep in debt himself — and yet, this warmth was something {name} didn't want to give up.

choices.text: Keep a polite distance — you can barely afford yourself  (focus / distance)
choices.result_text:
{name} stayed warm, but never let things go deeper.
She noticed the boundary too and took a small step back.
Caring costs something — and {name} couldn't afford the bill right now.
Whether that was wise restraint or lonely avoidance, he couldn't say.

choices.text: Come out with it — tell her about the ₩3B Gangnam dream  (honesty / vulnerability)
choices.result_text: The words came out. For the first time, in front of this person.

title: The Dream
description:
"Five years from now, I'll be in Gangnam. ₩3 billion in assets."
Daeun went still for a moment, then laughed quietly.
"...That's big. But why Gangnam specifically?"
The question stopped {name} cold.
There was no contempt in her eyes — just genuine curiosity.

choices.text: "So no one can look down on me." Say it straight  (understood / vulnerable)
choices.result_text:
{name} opened up for the first time — the moments when being poor felt like a mark of shame.
Daeun listened for a long time, then said quietly:
"...I get that. But even without Gangnam, you're not someone people should look down on."
No one had ever said that to him before.

choices.text: "Just the symbol of success, really." Brush it off  (distance kept / opportunity missed)
choices.result_text:
{name} smiled and kept his real answer buried.
She didn't press. The conversation stayed light and safe.
The less he showed, the less they grew closer.
The chance passed, by one small step.

title: Fork in the Road
description:
Daeun got a call from home. Her mother is unwell, and a stable position opened up at the local market back in her hometown.
"...I think I'm going to pack up here and go back. Seoul is just too much."
She looks at {name}. An unasked question lives in her eyes.

There's no reason to keep her in Seoul.
But answering that question — wasn't easy.

choices.text: "Don't go. Let's hold on here together" — reach for her
choices.result_text:
She was quiet for a moment. Then smiled softly.
"...Okay. I'll stay a little longer."
She didn't ask why. {name} didn't explain.

choices.text: Say nothing. Let her go  (focus on goal / regret·loss)
choices.result_text:
{name} couldn't open his mouth. Told himself: you can't afford to be anchored right now.
Daeun smiled faintly, said "Take care," and turned away.
After that, the late-night convenience store was once again a world of one.
The goal was sharp and clear — and one corner of the heart was permanently empty.

title: First Time Out
description:
She asked: "Want to go somewhere with me today?"

First time. Daeun outside the convenience store.

They ended up at a nearby tent bar — pojangmacha.
One bottle of soju. One serving of kimchi pancake.

She was different away from the counter.
A little more relaxed. A little more laughing.

He said "they should sell triangular kimbap here" and she burst out laughing.
A real laugh.

choices.text: "Today is enough." — Gangnam forgotten for a moment
choices.result_text:
They talked until late into the night.
None of it mattered — what they said.
On the way back, she reached for {name}'s hand first.
{name} said nothing. Nothing needed to be said.

choices.text: "Next time I'll take you somewhere better" — today feels like too little
choices.result_text: Today was today. Whether it was enough — not really sure.

title: The Reason at 3 A.M.
description:
3 A.M.

A message from Daeun.
"You awake? ...Just can't sleep. Not exactly struggling — just."

{name} stared at the screen, then looked out the window. Seoul doesn't go dark at 3 A.M.

₩3 billion was still far off. Time was always running short.

But right now, looking at this message — for the first time, it felt clear.
Why he was running.

choices.text: Reply: "Me too. Don't worry"
choices.result_text:
A short text exchange. Nothing important. Around 4 A.M. she fell asleep first.
{name} opened the laptop again. Wanted to win — for this person too.

choices.text: Send "Sleep well" — then open the laptop
choices.result_text: Can't afford to waver. But — why he's running felt a little clearer.

title: You and Gangnam
description:
Late. The sound of {name} clicking at a calculator woke Daeun.

She watched for a long time, then spoke quietly.
"...I get anxious sometimes."

{name} looked up, and she kept going.
"When you get to Gangnam... what happens to me?
You're the reason I stayed here,
but I don't know if the person who gets there will still want me."

The words hung in the air a long time.

{name} didn't know what to say.
There were things that couldn't be said yet — not until the right moment.

choices.text: "We go together. It only means something if you're with me."
choices.result_text:
Daeun looked at {name}'s face for a long time.
"...Do you mean that?"
"Yeah."
That night, he closed the calculator.
He counted something other than numbers.

choices.text: "When I get to Gangnam I'll treat you better. Bear with it for now."
choices.result_text: She smiled — but that smile was a little sad. {name} knew it too.

choices.text: "Honestly I don't know. I need to think about that too."
choices.result_text: Couldn't answer. That silence stayed with him a long time.

title: The Text That Never Sent
description:
Late at night, picked up the phone — and found himself in Daeun's contact.

Last message: 'Take care.' She'd sent it.
Below that — nothing.

He started typing.
'Hey, how have you been? You doing okay?'

Finger hovering over send.
Thinking about the ripple that one message would make in her life.

Deleted it.
Typed it again.
Deleted it again.

choices.text: Send it — a simple check-in is okay
choices.result_text:
A reply came back a little while later.
'Oh, hey. Doing fine :)'
That one emoji said a lot.
{name} set the phone down and looked out the window.

choices.text: Don't send it — going back into her life isn't right
choices.result_text:
Deleted.
The screen went black.
{name} stared at that dark screen for a long time.
I hope she's doing well. Truly. That's enough.
The most {name} could do, right now.

title: A Glimpse of Her
description:
Stumbled across it on social media.

A photo Daeun took back in her hometown.
In front of the mart. Side by side with her mom. One small potted plant. A bright smile.

'Doing just fine :)'

{name} looked at that photo for a long time.
She's okay. That thought arrived — and for some reason made the hollow feeling worse.
It only now fully landed that she was someone nowhere in Seoul anymore.

choices.text: Hit like — hope you're doing well. I'll do the same
choices.result_text:
He tapped like.
A moment later, a notification: 'Daeun liked your post.'

No short comment. {name} said nothing either.
That was enough. That was the end.

choices.text: Scroll past — pretend you didn't see it
choices.result_text:
{name} scrolled down.
The next post was a crypto ad.
Life continued.

Only the things that never quite arrived stayed behind.

title: A Rented Room in Winter
description:
Daeun dropped by often. Always with something in her hands.
A few eggs. Spinach. Tofu.

{name} would be staring at an investment screen and she'd reach over and touch the frame of his glasses.
"Your eyes are going to give out." That had become something they just said.

They weren't a couple. But just friends didn't quite cover it either — there was something more.
Neither of them put that line into words.

Somewhere along the way, her being here stopped feeling strange.
Whether that was good, or just habit — he wasn't sure.

choices.text: Decide to just cook something together tonight
choices.result_text: They dug through the fridge together. Nothing decent to work with — but that kind of evening wasn't bad.

choices.text: "I still can't give you much yet — is that okay?"
choices.result_text:
Daeun paused for a moment. "I'm not asking for that."
The words were plain. Something still unnamed sat quietly between them.

title: The End of Waiting
description:
A message from Daeun.
"Can we talk for a bit?"

A side table at a pojangmacha. Two shots of soju.

"I've been thinking about it for a long time. It's not that you're a bad person —
but I have my own life too. I don't want waiting to become my life."

{name} had things to say. Things he should have said.
It felt too late for them now.

choices.text: "I'm sorry. You're right." Accept it.
choices.result_text:
She stood up. "I hope things work out for you. I mean that."
It sounded like the truth. That made it worse.

{name} sat there for a long time after she left.
The words 'just wait a little longer' — this was where they led.

choices.text: "Even now — I can change." Try to hold on.
choices.result_text:
She looked at {name} for a moment.
"It's not about you changing. I chose to wait too. I'm just tired of it."

That was the more honest answer.
{name} couldn't find a word to say.

title: The In-Between Distance
description:
They'd been seeing each other less.
No clear starting point for when.
No plans made. No avoidance either.
Just — both getting busy.

Today he ran into her on the street.
"Oh, hey." A long silence after that.
This had become their default.

They never officially ended things, so things never ended.
They never tried to continue, so things never continued.

choices.text: "Where does this leave us?" Ask her directly.
choices.result_text:
She thought for a while. Then: "...I don't know. Me neither."

Both of them not knowing — that was itself a kind of answer.
After that day, neither reached out. That was the answer too.

choices.text: "You doing okay?" Let it pass.
choices.result_text:
"Yeah, doing fine."
And they each went their separate way.

He didn't look back. More accurately — he didn't have the nerve to.
The silence from that night of 'I'm not sure' —
it ended like this.
